GNOME 50 emits this diagnostic on otherwise healthy input-source startup. Separate checks require gsd-keyboard to remain alive and the configured Rime source to be readable.

GNOME 50 can emit this assertion while the transient GDM greeter user's media-keys service exits after a manual desktop login. The rule excludes the installed user's UID, while the same action must still prove the real user session and GNOME Shell remain healthy.

One GNOME 50 startup assertion was observed during automatic login; the same ISO and case passed on rerun. The gate separately requires the installed user's media-keys service and process to remain active, so a broken service still fails.

GNOME 50 can issue two identical calls through a closing D-Bus connection while gsd-sharing shuts down in an automatic-login session. Separate health evidence requires the user's GNOME Shell, settings-daemon services, keyring, extensions, and input sources to remain operational.
GNOME 50 can emit this transient window-stack diagnostic while the Shell remains healthy. Separate checks cover window activation, extension state, SPICE resize, and the live Shell process.

DING on GTK 4.22 can emit this one transient accessibility assertion while closing or replacing a GTK popover. The same diagnostic was observed with DING 97; its desktop context menu and Open in Terminal were verified on the host. Separate ISO UI checks require DING to remain alive and verify icons, background actions, desktop shortcuts, extension state, and GNOME Shell health.
